title: ailang fmt — Canonical AILANG Source Formatter (Phase 1)

model_routing.billing: quota-bucket anthropic (no metered spend, no external calls)

hard_constraints: Fail closed on comments (exit 2, byte-identical file), parse errors, unsupported/unknown AST nodes, and write failures. No fallback to original source.
Do NOT modify internal/ast/print.go or its JSON golden output — byte-for-byte untouched. It is a golden-test contract, NOT source-formatting infrastructure.
Do NOT change the grammar or any spelling accepted by the parser. No --strict-syntax change.

Exhaustive AST visitor: every concrete node kind gets a source printer or an explicit unsupported-error path. NEVER call existing AST String() methods as a fallback (they are debug renderings, not precedence-safe source).
Parentheses are precedence-driven: the AST has no ParenExpr node (verified V20), so Phase 1 reconstructs parens from parent precedence + syntactic position; source-only redundant parens are removed.
explicit let..in stays explicit: nil-Body lets print as newline statements in their sequence; non-nil-Body lets print as `let name = value in body`. No source-spelling side table.

Canonical sequence form: braced newline-per-expression, final value expression bare, NO sequence semicolons. Two-space indent, LF output, exactly one final newline, one blank line between top-level decls, original AST order (module, imports, decls) — no reordering.

Atomic multi-file --write: validate ALL inputs (preflight+parse+print+round-trip) in memory FIRST; replace each file individually via same-directory temp + os.Rename, preserving each original file mode. Cross-file crash atomicity is NOT claimed.
Exit codes: 0 success / all canonical; 1 --check found non-canonical (no operational error); 2 usage/read/comment-preflight/parse/print/round-trip/write error.
No new diagnostic code. Human-readable path-qualified stderr errors only.
internal/lexer opt-in comment scan must NOT change Lexer.NextToken() output used by the parser — byte-for-byte behaviorally unchanged.
Formatter consumes only parsed AST + fixed Options. No type checker, elaborator, filesystem, env, or wall clock.

velocity.basis: Doc-provided estimates (M1 2d, M2 0.5d, M3 1d, M4 0.5d). No padding per mission directive.

ast_node_surface.note: Exhaustive coverage required. All concrete node kinds enumerated from internal/ast (2026-07-18).

features.name: Exhaustive AST-to-Source Printer
features.description: New internal/format package: a document/token builder (indent, hard-line, soft-line, group primitives) and precedence-aware exhaustive visitor over every concrete declaration, expression, type, pattern, effect, test, and property node. Unknown/nil-required/ast.Error nodes fail loudly. String/char/quasiquote literals go through one canonical escaping routine — never String() fallback. Emits func.Source(program, Options) and lays down canonical-form goldens.
files: internal/format/precedence.go (operator precedence table + parent-context parens rule)
acceptance_criteria: Canonical statement sequence: braces + newline-per-expression, final expression bare, zero sequence semicolons.
Single-expression function bodies print `= expr`; multi-expression ast.Block bodies print a braced newline block; a one-expression normalization wrapper does NOT force braces unless grammar requires.
Two-space indent, LF, exactly one final newline, one blank line between top-level decls, original AST order for module/imports/decls (no reordering of imports, symbols, cases, fields, decls).
Parentheses reconstructed from parent precedence + syntactic position; redundant source-only parens removed (no ast.ParenExpr exists, V20).
Every concrete AST node kind has a source-printer test OR an explicit unsupported-error test; NO debug String() fallback anywhere.

String/char/quasiquote literals emit via ONE escaping routine; malformed/unsupported literal payloads return an error rather than String() fallback; quasiquote template contents are never reinterpreted.
Printer depends only on AST + Options: no type checker, elaborator, filesystem, env, or wall-clock access.
features.notes: internal/format package: doc builder + precedence-aware exhaustive visitor over every concrete AST node; single canonical escaping routine; per-node coverage tests + canonical-layout goldens. Cons re-emitted infix; parens precedence-driven; block-vs-bare body fidelity handled. All 21 comment-free examples round-trip+idempotent. Commit ab98f4b98.

features.name: CLI and Transactional File Handling
features.description: Add `fmt` case to cmd/ailang dispatch with help text. Implement default single-file stdout mode, --write (1+ files), --check (1+ files), mutual exclusion of --write/--check, argument validation, and exit codes 0/1/2. Multi-file --write buffers and fully validates every file in memory (preflight+parse+print+round-trip) before replacing any; implement an unexported same-directory temp-file + os.Rename helper in cmd/ailang that preserves each original file mode (no shared helper exists — V19).
files: cmd/ailang/fmt.go (fmt subcommand: flag parsing, stdout/--write/--check modes, exit codes, path-qualified diagnostics, unexported atomic-write helper)
acceptance_criteria: `ailang fmt file.ail` emits canonical source to stdout and leaves the file unchanged (exactly one file in stdout mode).
`ailang fmt --write a.ail b.ail` changes NO file if preflight/parse/print/round-trip fails for ANY input; each replacement is individually atomic (same-dir temp + os.Rename) and preserves file mode.
`ailang fmt --check` exits 0 when all inputs canonical, exits 1 and lists drifted paths when formatting differs, exits 2 on operational/usage errors; NEVER writes.
Canonical means byte-equal to formatter output INCLUDING final newline.
--write and --check are mutually exclusive; zero files, multiple files in stdout mode, or both flags = usage error (exit 2).
Inputs processed in argument order; diagnostics deterministic and path-qualified.
Atomic-write helper is unexported, lives in cmd/ailang, stages a same-directory temp, preserves original mode, calls os.Rename — no shared helper reused.
features.notes: cmd/ailang/fmt.go: stdout/--write/--check, mutual exclusion, arg validation, exit codes 0/1/2. In-memory validate-all-before-write; unexported same-dir temp + os.Rename atomic helper preserving mode. Behaviorally proven with worktree binary. Commit 2fd01036c.

features.name: Idempotence and Corpus Round-Trip
features.description: Property/corpus test harness. Byte-idempotence property (fmt(fmt(x))==fmt(x)) and structural round-trip (Parse(fmt(x))==Parse(x)) via go-cmp ignoring positions/spans/file paths only — NOT textual equality of debug String(). Run across every comment-free examples/**/*.ail file plus parser formatter fixtures. Commented examples partitioned explicitly: detect, assert exit 2, assert unchanged bytes. Focused fixtures for the three equivalent separator spellings must format to identical text; explicit let..in proven to remain explicit and round-trip.
files: internal/format/roundtrip_test.go (idempotence + structural round-trip property tests, go-cmp with explicit ignored metadata)
internal/format/corpus_test.go (walk comment-free examples/**/*.ail + parser fixtures; partition commented -> exit-2 + unchanged-bytes)
internal/format/separators_test.go (three-separator-spelling identical-output fixtures + explicit let..in stays-explicit round-trip)
acceptance_criteria: Idempotence property test proves fmt(fmt(x))==fmt(x) byte-for-byte over generated AST cases AND the formatter-eligible example corpus.
Structural round-trip test proves Parse(fmt(x))==Parse(x) over every comment-free example and dedicated fixture, ignoring ONLY positions/spans/file paths (go-cmp, not String()).
Equation-semicolon, braced-semicolon, and braced-newline fixtures format to the SAME newline-per-statement braced form.
Explicit `let ... in` formats as `let ... in` (non-nil Body preserved) and structurally round-trips.
Every commented example is detected, exits 2, and remains byte-identical (partitioned from the round-trip set).
Existing parser R1/R2 equivalence and corpus AST-diff tests remain green (unchanged).
features.notes: Idempotence + structural round-trip property tests (go-cmp ignoring pos/span) over generated cases + corpus (21 comment-free files formatted; 372 commented detected). Three-separator identical-output + explicit let..in stays-explicit fixtures. Commented -> exit2 + byte-identical CLI test. Parser R1/R2 + corpus AST-diff green. Commit 3021c6f23.

features.name: Comment Safety Gate and Documentation
features.description: Implement HasComments as a lossless lexical preflight (opt-in trivia-emitting scan mode in internal/lexer that does NOT change NextToken output). Distinguish real comment introducers from string/char/regex/quasiquote contents — never substring matching. Marker tests for leading/trailing/floating comments and comment-like text inside literals/quasiquotes. Document Phase 1 refusal and Phase 2 attachment model in CLI help + guides. Run make test, make fmt, and example verification target.
files: internal/lexer/lexer.go (opt-in trivia/comment-emitting scan mode; NextToken behavior unchanged)
docs/docs/guides/ (or CLI help): Phase 1 refusal + Phase 2 attachment-model documentation
acceptance_criteria: HasComments detects any real source comment before parsing and is lossless (comment introducers vs literal/quasiquote/regex contents), never substring-based.
Opt-in lexer scan mode leaves default NextToken() output byte-for-byte behaviorally unchanged (parser-visible tokens unaffected).
Marker tests distinguish actual comments from comment-like text in strings/quasiquotes (leading, trailing, floating, string-contained, quasiquote-contained).
Phase 1 refusal (exit 2, stderr `path: comments are not yet supported by ailang fmt`, no write) documented in CLI help/guides; Phase 2 attachment model documented as separately-scheduled.
internal/ast/print.go and its JSON golden output remain byte-for-byte untouched.
`make test`, `make fmt`, and the repository example-verification target pass.
features.notes: HasComments lossless preflight via opt-in internal/lexer/comment_scan.go (NextToken byte-for-byte unchanged, proven by test). Leading/trailing/floating + string/char/quasiquote-contained marker tests. Docs: reference/formatter.md + sidebar + CLI --help. make test/verify-examples/check-file-sizes all green. print.go untouched. Commit d5fa52606.

implementation_plan.day_3_afternoon_day_4_morning: M3: idempotence + corpus round-trip harness + separator/let-in fixtures.

release_gate_tests: Idempotence property test: fmt(fmt(x))==fmt(x) byte-for-byte over generated AST cases + eligible example corpus.
Structural round-trip: Parse(fmt(x))==Parse(x) over every comment-free examples/**/*.ail + fixtures, ignoring positions/spans/paths only.
Three separator spellings (equation-semicolon / braced-semicolon / braced-newline) format to identical newline-per-statement braced text.
Explicit let..in stays explicit and structurally round-trips.
Every commented file: detected -> exit 2 -> byte-identical; literal/quasiquote comment-like text NOT misdetected.
Every concrete AST node kind has a printer test or explicit unsupported-error test (no String() fallback).
internal/ast/print.go + JSON goldens byte-for-byte untouched; parser R1/R2 + corpus AST-diff tests green.
make test, make fmt, example-verification target all pass.

corpus_notes.note: The comment-free set (~49) is the round-trip/idempotence corpus; the commented remainder (~344) is the exit-2/unchanged-bytes partition. Counts are advisory — M3 must compute the partition programmatically via HasComments, not hard-code these numbers.

top_risk: Printer completeness: the AST surface is broad (40+ concrete node kinds); a single precedence, literal, pattern, or declaration omission breaks round-trip even when simple sequence examples look correct. M1 exhaustive coverage + M3 corpus/property tests are the release gate.
